q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT DISTINCT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS totalVisits FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS totalVisits FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE (f1.drinker <> f2.drinker AND f1.totalVisits = f2.totalVisits AND f1.drinker > f2.drinker)

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they use different conditions in the WHERE clause. Q1 uses 'f1.drinker < f2.drinker', while Q2 uses 'f1.drinker > f2.drinker'. This means that Q1 will return pairs where the first drinker is lexicographically smaller than the second, whereas Q2 will return pairs where the first drinker is lexicographically larger than the second.
